FIFO and batch-class share one global admission clock; at most four 64-byte blocks enter all channel controllers per paper cycle, while each channel independently enforces the 32-entry read queue and 32-entry write buffer
configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini cmd_queue_size=8; the request-level controller bounds each bank command queue to the same depth

FIFO selects one Edge/Input/Weight/Output port per admission cycle, admits up to four consecutive blocks, and bounds the uncoordinated in-flight row windows to the four Figure 9 request sources; batch-class assembles batch-local Edge > Input > Weight > Output streams with same batch/class open-row continuation

HyGCN HPCA 2020 Figure 9 shows four concurrent Edge, Input, Weight, and Output request sources; Section 4.5.2 says the uncoordinated requests are handled sequentially and the coordinator assembles them into continuous batch-local streams before low-bit remapping
derived from the paper profile peak interface width: floor(256 bytes/cycle divided by 64 bytes/block)

after.command_issue_interval_formula: ceil(tCK / model_cycle_ns); each physical channel issues row commands on its own replicated DRAMSim3 command lane
after.command_model: request completion is measured from actual READ/WRITE issue; row conflicts explicitly schedule PRE then ACT before the data command, while tWR/tRTP/tRAS and PRE-to-ACT constrain recovery
after.read_to_precharge_formula: ceil((AL + tRTP) * tCK / model_cycle_ns); bundled HBM config omits tRTP, so DRAMSim3 default tRTP=5 applies
after.read_to_write_formula: ceil((RL + burst_cycle - WL + tRTRS) * tCK / model_cycle_ns)
after.transfer_note: burst/block transfer is modeled separately by transfer_cycles, so BL is not duplicated in CL/CWL completion latency

after.policy: every admission records per-channel read/write occupancy before and after mutation; a terminal zero snapshot lets the validator infer all intervening dispatch counts from zero and independently recompute peaks, capacity violations, totals, histograms, edge samples, and checksum

changed_paths.after: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Section 4.5.2 executes requests batch-by-batch: all requests from the current batch, including its lower-priority classes, precede high-priority requests from the next batch
one row-sized block span stays in one bank, then the collapsed mapping advances channel and bank fields in the order represented by rorabgbachco
changed_paths.before: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini uses address_mapping=rorabgbachco; the request-level row-first baseline preserves full-row locality before distributing rows across channels and reports the collapsed mapping formula in source and tests

changed_paths.after: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini selects address_mapping=rorabgbachco. The collapsed request-level baseline therefore keeps every contiguous row span in one bank; it does not add an unsupported adjacent-bank striping factor.
changed_paths.before: The review-v3 baseline used kUncoordinatedBankInterleave=2. This version preserves that baseline value for comparability but moves it into configuration and reports it explicitly. DRAMSim3 enables a second HBM command per cycle when read/write classes differ; the two-bank striping is only a request-level width approximation, not a claim that DRAMSim3 pairs adjacent banks.

changed_paths.after: HyGCN reports 256 GB/s HBM1. The bundled DRAMSim3 HBM1_4Gb_x128 profile is one 8-channel 128 GB/s stack, so the paper profile replicates that timing and queue topology across two stacks rather than inventing a faster per-channel command rate.
configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini sets unified_queue=False and trans_queue_size=32; DRAMSim3 therefore allocates an independent 32-entry read_queue and 32-entry write_buffer in every channel controller
